title: Checkout migration review
userText: We need to migrate checkout from a legacy session-based flow to a new payment orchestration service. Compare three rollout strategies, show the risks for inventory reservation and coupon rollback, and propose a phased plan that support, backend, and frontend can all review.
assistantText:
## Recommendation

Use a shadow-write rollout first, then move to cohort-based traffic shifting. Do not start with a big-bang migration because checkout has coupled failure modes across payment authorization, inventory reservation, coupon redemption, and customer support recovery.

## Strategies compared

| Strategy | Benefit | Main risk | Best use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Big-bang cutover | Fastest cleanup of legacy code | Any payment or inventory mismatch affects all buyers | Only after repeated rehearsals |
| Cohort traffic shifting | Easy to pause and roll back | Requires dual metrics and support routing | Good default rollout mechanism |
| Shadow-write first | Finds data mismatches before buyers are exposed | Does not prove payment provider behavior under real traffic | Best first phase |

## Failure modes

- Payment authorized but inventory reservation fails, creating a refund path.
- Inventory reserved but payment authorization times out, creating stuck stock.
- Coupon redeemed in the new service but rollback only happens in the legacy session.
- Support tooling reads legacy order state while the buyer sees new orchestration state.
- Retry jobs double-submit payment capture when idempotency keys are not shared.

## Phased rollout

1. Instrument the legacy checkout with correlation IDs shared across payment, coupon, inventory, and order records.
2. Run shadow-write mode for the orchestration service while legacy remains source of truth.
3. Compare shadow results against legacy outcomes with a mismatch dashboard.
4. Enable staff-only real checkout through the new service.
5. Shift 1% of low-risk traffic, excluding high-value carts and cross-border payment methods.
6. Increase cohorts only when payment, inventory, coupon, and support metrics stay within thresholds.
7. Freeze legacy write paths after a full business cycle with no critical mismatches.

## Review matrix

| Reviewer | What to inspect | Approval signal |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | Idempotency, retry, state machine transitions | No duplicate capture or stuck reservation in replay tests |
| Frontend | Error state copy, retry UX, loading transitions | Buyers can recover without support for known transient failures |
| Support | Order lookup, refund explanation, manual release path | Agents can explain and resolve every partial failure state |
| Data | Dashboard joins and mismatch definitions | Shadow-write mismatch rate is visible and actionable |

## Rollback plan

- Keep legacy checkout as source of truth until cohort phase is stable.
- Store orchestration decisions with reversible state transitions.
- Disable traffic shifting with a feature flag, not a deploy.
- Reconcile coupon and inventory side effects before refund automation runs.

## Decision

Start with shadow-write. Move to cohort shifting only after mismatch dashboards prove that the new orchestration service agrees with legacy outcomes across payment, inventory, coupon, and support views.
